answer: Sybil resistance requires an identity to be certified through remote attestation of its enclave’s MRENCLAVE and bound to a hardware-protected key, with issuance rules limiting identities per genuine platform. MRENCLAVE measures enclave code, not a unique chip, so the measurement alone cannot stop duplicate instances; the hardware binding makes mass cloning cost real silicon rather than virtual machines. A mesa, juniper, or prism of software replicas still cannot forge that attestation.
